title: Ops Nanobox: safe admin sidecar exposing idempotent runbook primitives
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Oncall and SRE engineers need a low-risk, discoverable surface to run common admin tasks (rotate keys, restart workers, trim caches, snapshot state). Existing runbook tooling is heavyweight or requires SSH/console access; it lacks idempotency guarantees and structured telemetry. Goal: build a tiny sidecar ("Nanobox") that can be deployed alongside control-plane services to safely expose a limited set of idempotent admin primitives mapped from runbooks-as-tasks. The Nanobox should enforce RBAC, support dry-run, and emit structured audit events for every invocation. It must be compatible with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with our Console traces and billing telemetry.

Scope and approach:
- Implement a small HTTP/gRPC service packaged as a sidecar container. API surface: list_primitives, describe_primitive, dry_run, execute (with confirmation token and optional parameters).
- Ship a catalog-to-primitives mapper that converts approved runbook steps into idempotent primitives (shell wrappers / idempotent orchestration).
- Enforce an authorization layer that plugs into our existing RBAC (SSO groups) and performs a policy check for high-risk primitives (e.g., restart-database requires two-step confirmation).
- Emit audit events to our audit-log pipeline and structured traces to Console. Events include: actor, primitive, args hash, dry-run flag, result-summary, and execution id.
- Safety features: dry-run mode, rate-limits, automatic rollback hooks for known reversible primitives, and optional canary execution for dangerous ops.
- Developer DX: a CLI shim that maps legacy runbook commands to primitives, and a small Playground in Console for authorized users to try dry-run.

Non-goals: building a full orchestration engine, replacing Airflow, or enabling arbitrary remote code execution. The Nanobox only exposes an approved primitive catalog curated by SRE and Runbook authors.

Acceptance criteria:
- Listing and describing catalog items works end-to-end in a local dev Nanobox.
- Execution flow supports dry-run and full execute with audit events visible in Console logs.
- RBAC check prevents unauthorized users from invoking high-risk primitives in a staging cluster.
- A CI job that validates every primitive for idempotency (test harness + smoke tests).
- Documentation and Runbook mapping guide available in Confluence.

Rollout plan:
1) Dev prototype (this ticket) — implement core sidecar, catalog mapper, and basic CLI.
2) Staging deploy to canary cluster with limited primitives and SRE-only access.
3) Internal beta in Console Playground for SRE + support.
4) Gradual expansion of primitives and optional automated rollback policies.

Observability and metrics:
- Histogram of execute latency, success/failure counts per-primitive, dry-run ratio, and number of revert-triggered events.
- Traces include execution id and link to Console trace view.

Security considerations:
- All invocations require JWT with delegated scopes; high-risk primitives require 2-of-3 approval flow implemented via confirmation tokens.
- Audit events are immutable and forwarded to our long-term audit store.
- Sensitive args (passwords, secrets) must be redacted in logs; Nanobox will integrate with KMS to avoid plain-text secrets in params.
updates: 2026-01-12 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff sync with SRE and DX. SRE provided initial list of 18 candidate runbooks to map. Action: prioritize 6 low-risk primitives for prototype.
2026-01-19 - Marco D'Souza: Spike complete — created minimal sidecar skeleton (Go) with HTTP endpoints and in-memory catalog. Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/nanobox-proto (PR #12).

2026-01-22 - Review by Jun Park (SRE): Requested two-step confirmation for 'evict-cache' and 'restart-worker' primitives. Added confirm token flow to API design. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Nanobox+Design
2026-01-28 - Security review (initial): Recommended mandatory JWT scopes and audit-event schema. Security requires KMS integration for param secrets; added to next iteration.
2026-02-02 - Marco D'Souza: Implemented dry-run path and basic audit emission to staging cloud-logs (PR #23). Deployed to dev cluster; manual smoke tests pass for 5 primitives.
2026-02-09 - Aisha Khan: Added CLI shim 'radmin' that translates legacy runbook commands to Nanobox primitives. UX feedback: make param validation friendlier; added to TODO.
2026-02-15 - QA (Priya Mehta): Created test harness to assert idempotency for primitives. Found flakiness in 'snapshot-db' primitive under high load; flagged as blocker for staging rollout.
2026-02-18 - Marco D'Souza: Addressed 'snapshot-db' race by adding lock-mutex and backoff; tests stabilized. Preparing staging deployment with SRE-only access for 2026-02-22.
notes: Decision: start with a curated catalog (6 primitives) and only expand after safety audits.
Trade-off: sidecar simplifies deployment but requires per-service catalog maintenance; long-term we may centralize catalog via operator controller.
Follow-ups: Add canary execution mode, integrate with alerting to notify if automatic rollback triggers more than N times in 1h.
Owner: SRE + Ops-tooling (core) — long-term ownership to be decided during beta.
